capabilities: Map multi-key sequences, leaders, and modified keys to Obsidian commands
Apply mappings across tabs, sidebars, and other app views
Store mappings in a vault-local .vimrc-style config file
Start from a LazyVim-inspired starter config
Discover command IDs via the developer console
disambiguation: Not a Vim editor emulator; it only triggers Obsidian commands, while Obsidian's own Vim mode handles in-editor text editing.
extras: Users must enable Obsidian's built-in Vim key bindings and unassign any conflicting hotkeys; only nmap and let mapleader lines in the config file are parsed.
intentEvidence: This plugin extends Obsidian's built-in Vim mode; it does not replace it.
problem: Obsidian hotkeys only take single key combinations, and built-in Vim mode applies only inside the editor, leaving no multi-key command mappings for tabs, sidebars, and other views.

relations.evidence: Mini Vimrc complements this plugin well
a ready-to-adapt, LazyVim-inspired starter based on LazyVim key mappings

summary: Vim-style key-mapping plugin that binds multi-key sequences and leader keys to any Obsidian command, working app-wide.
